clue.text: Carry weapon with aim to threaten

parts.note: to port arms is to carry a rifle diagonally across the body, so port means carry a weapon
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Someone shoulders a gun and takes aim in a menacing way.
explanation.definitionFit: Clouds that portend a storm foreshadow it, so the verb means to signal or menace as an omen.

clue.text: Unpolluted water is produced by River Board

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
a table is a board, as in 'bed and board' or a board laid for a meal

explanation.surface: Clean drinking water is supplied by the local River Board authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River Board' looks like one official body; it is two pieces. 'water is produced by' is the link, describing the clean water the answer qualifies.
explanation.definitionFit: Potable water is fit to drink, which means it is clean and free of contamination.

clue.text: Carried away over top of Olympus to elevated retreat of predator

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the next one

parts.note: rapt means carried away, entranced

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter
in a down answer, raising a word makes it read from the bottom up

parts.note: a lair is a hideaway or retreat

explanation.surface: Someone is swept off up Mount Olympus to a lofty hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns LAIR upwards into RIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Raptorial describes birds of prey and other hunters, so the adjective means belonging to a predator.

clue.text: Editor accepts pieces, to do this

indicators.note: the editor's letters take in the pieces, so one word holds the other

parts.note: chessmen are pieces, so men can mean pieces

explanation.surface: An editor takes in bits of text in order to correct them.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back at the editor: correcting text is exactly what an editor does.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct and improve a text is the editor's job, which is what the verb means.

clue.text: Run down turbulent rapids on time

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece rests on the one beneath it
turbulent water is churned up, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A boat races down through wild rapids against the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run down' looks like the action of the boat; it is the definition, meaning belittle. 'turbulent' rearranges RAPIDS into DISPAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To belittle or speak slightingly of something is to run it down.

clue.text: Reached top of Cape and took a breather

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
to take a breather is to pause for rest

explanation.surface: A walker gets to the summit of a headland and pauses for breath.
explanation.definitionFit: To crest a hill is to reach its summit, so the past tense means arrived at the peak.

clue.text: Garment worn by Society in Strand

indicators.note: a garment worn by someone wraps around them, so these letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: a coat is a garment

explanation.surface: Fashionable people wear a particular garment along the Strand in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strand' looks like the London street, but here it is the shore. The Strand is a famous street in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is a beach or shoreline, the land that borders the sea.

clue.text: Regard leading batsman as a major surprise

parts.note: to eye something is to regard or look at it
in cricket the opener is one of the two batsmen who start an innings

explanation.surface: A spectator views the top-order batsman as an astonishing find.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that opens one's eyes is a revelation, a startling discovery.

clue.text: A nameless giant reared in Siberian forest

indicators.note: something reared stands up, so in a down clue these letters read upwards
N is short for name, so nameless means the letter N is dropped

explanation.surface: An unnamed giant was brought up in the woods of Siberia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' takes N from GIANT to leave GIAT; 'reared' turns A GIAT upwards into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The taiga is the vast coniferous forest belt of Siberia and the far north.

clue.text: Fine leather is suitable to put on family

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece put on another sits above it

parts.note: 'that does' means that is suitable or will serve
kin means family

explanation.surface: A tasteful leather garment is fitting for the family to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Doeskin is soft leather made from the hide of a deer or lamb.

clue.text: Headgear that accommodates crown with ease, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said aloud, signalling a word that sounds alike

parts.note: a hairpiece fits snugly over the crown of a bald head

explanation.surface: A hat is said to fit comfortably over the top of the head.
explanation.walkthrough: A hairpiece sits easily on the crown; the answer, a sun helmet, sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A topee is a lightweight pith helmet worn against the sun, a kind of hat.

clue.text: Injury inflicted by the Serpentine

parts.note: the Serpentine, a lake in London's Hyde Park, is read as a snaky creature, which wounds with its fangs

explanation.surface: Someone is hurt in an accident at the Serpentine lake in Hyde Park.
explanation.walkthrough: The Serpentine is a lake in Hyde Park, London; read as 'the serpentine one' it is a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound made by the fangs of a serpent is exactly what the phrase describes.

clue.text: Transmission to select on inferior thoroughfare

indicators.note: in an across clue a piece put on another follows it

parts.note: in Britain a B-road is a minor road, lesser than an A-road
to cast actors is to select them for parts

explanation.surface: A broadcaster chooses to air a programme about a minor street.
explanation.walkthrough: British roads are graded A (main) and B (secondary), so a B-road is the inferior thoroughfare.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme sent out over radio or television is a transmission.

clue.text: Tricky outcome of pawn offensive

parts.note: P is the chess notation for a pawn
rank means foul-smelling or offensive

explanation.surface: A chess pawn's attack produces a crafty result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like a chess attack, but here it is the adjective, foul.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical joke is the result of trickery, so a mischievous trick fits.

clue.text: Poet's English work rejected

indicators.note: rejected things are sent back, so this word is turned round

parts.note: toil means hard work

explanation.surface: A poet's English composition was turned down by the publisher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' reads as 'Poet is', so the definition is the poet; the work is sent back by the publisher, which is the turning signal.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot was the poet of The Waste Land, and George Eliot also wrote verse.

clue.text: Romance, we hear, with man on board is ending

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by its sound when spoken

parts.note: a romance is a story, a tale
a chessman on the board is a piece

explanation.surface: A love affair with a sailor aboard ship is coming to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' suggests a sailor; it is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailpiece is a final part added at the end of something, such as a book.

clue.text: It's blown up in the Swiss mountains

definitions.text: It's blown up in the Swiss mountains

parts.words: It's blown up in the Swiss mountains
parts.note: suggests an explosion in the Alps, but describes a long wooden instrument that herdsmen blow there

explanation.surface: Something is detonated high in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown up' means exploded on the surface, but here it means played by blowing, high up.
explanation.definitionFit: The long wooden horn played by Alpine herdsmen is sounded by blowing in the Swiss Alps.

clue.text: King procures ensemble initially for herald

indicators.note: ensemble means all together, so the pieces are mixed as one pool

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king hires a musical group to act as his herald.
explanation.walkthrough: R is put first in the pool ('initially') and mixed with PROCURES.
explanation.definitionFit: A forerunner who comes before and announces what follows is a herald.

clue.text: Unattached guys may be ready to go on

definitions.text: Unattached guys may be ready to go on

parts.words: Unattached guys may be ready to go on
parts.note: tent guy ropes come loose from their pegs, while clothes ready to put on are sold ready-made

explanation.surface: Single men are eager to go out on the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guys' looks like men; it means guy ropes, freed from their tent pegs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-made clothes bought off a rack are ready to wear, ready to put on.

clue.text: Crawler impelled one to pull out

indicators.note: pulling something out of shape rearranges it, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A grovelling person forced someone else to withdraw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawler' looks like a sycophant; it is a many-legged creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A millipede is a many-legged arthropod that crawls along the ground.

clue.text: Covered up blunder, having been prompted

parts.note: to muff is to bungle, and a muff is a blunder
led means guided or prompted

explanation.surface: A mistake was concealed after someone was nudged to hide it.
explanation.definitionFit: Muffled means wrapped up or covered, as in muffled against the cold.

clue.text: Renewal of vamp's appeal before judge? Just the reverse

indicators.note: the clue says the appeal comes before the judge, then tells us to swap that order

parts.note: a referee, ref, judges a match
it is old slang for sex appeal, which a vamp has

explanation.surface: A seductress pleads her case before a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appeal before judge' sounds like a court case, but the appeal is a vamp's allure; 'Just the reverse' swaps the stated order, putting the judge first.
explanation.definitionFit: A refit is a renovation or overhaul, a renewal of equipment.

clue.text: Battlefield's operational centre

definitions.meaning: a ... of war is the area where fighting takes place
an operating ... is the hospital room where surgery is done

explanation.surface: A battlefield's command headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a region of combat and the room where surgeons operate.

clue.text: Discontented — or satisfied?

definitions.meaning: being sick and tired of things, fed to the back teeth
read literally as having been fed to the full, sated

explanation.surface: Unhappy, or is it content?
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means weary and unhappy, while read word by word it means well fed.

clue.text: Does, for example, inserting Times leader discourage?

indicators.note: inserting means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: does, female deer, are examples of deer

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Is a Times editorial putting people off?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like the verb; it is the plural of doe.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter someone is to put them off or dissuade them.

clue.text: Is it about a foot in front of bench?

definitions.text: Is it about a foot in front of bench?

parts.words: Is it about a foot in front of bench?
parts.note: suggests a measurement in a law court, but describes footwear around a foot, with bench meaning a court

explanation.surface: Is the distance from the judge's bench about twelve inches?
explanation.walkthrough: 'about a foot' looks like a length; footwear goes about a foot. Bench is a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: A court shoe is a plain low-cut woman's shoe without fastenings, a pump.

clue.text: Endlessly outshine in film parts

indicators.note: a word without its ends loses its first and last letters

parts.note: to eclipse something is to outshine it

explanation.surface: To shine beyond all limits in roles in movies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' looks like 'forever', but it trims the first and last letters from ECLIPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Short excerpts from films are called clips.

clue.text: Raffles, say, as openings to train helpers in extracting funds

indicators.note: openings to words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A trainer teaches assistants how to get money out of people.
explanation.walkthrough: Raffles is the gentleman burglar of E. W. Hornung's stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A. J. Raffles is a famous fictional cracksman, a stealer of jewels.

clue.text: Fables about animal's risky situations

indicators.note: about means around, so these letters go around the other piece

parts.note: fables are fictions, lies
an otter is an animal; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Fairy tales are told about a creature's dangerous predicaments.
explanation.definitionFit: Ventures whose outcome depends on chance are gambles, things left to luck.

clue.text: One new option to sell data for computer

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
in finance a put is an option to sell shares at a set price

explanation.surface: A fresh choice to sell information about a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Information fed into a machine for processing is what it takes in.

clue.text: Animal home surrounded by others gets less light

indicators.note: one piece is surrounded by the other, so it sits inside

parts.note: other animal homes, after the first, are dens
Noah's ark housed the animals

explanation.surface: A creature's shelter, hemmed in by others, gets little daylight.
explanation.walkthrough: The ark is one animal home; 'others' are further animal homes, dens.
explanation.definitionFit: When the sky darkens it grows dimmer and has less brightness.

clue.text: Urge fee revision for person flying from home

indicators.note: revision means the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone requests a change of fee for a passenger flying out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' suggests air travel; here it means fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who flees their country to escape danger is seeking asylum abroad.
